description: Cover letter from a posting and a short background: it uses only the supplied achievements and figures, does not claim the posting's nice-to-have tool the applicant has never used, addresses the named manager, and avoids the 'I am excited to apply' opener, adjective stacking and a generic closer.
prompt: I'm applying for the data analyst job in posting.md. My background is in background.md. Write the cover letter, one page, to the hiring manager. Save it to out/letter.md.

files.posting.md:
Data Analyst, Northgate Library Network (full-time)

Northgate runs 14 branch libraries. You will report to Hannah Okoye, head of data and planning.

You will:
- build and maintain monthly usage reports for branch managers
- clean and join data from our loans system and the door counters
- answer ad hoc questions from the board

We need: SQL, a dashboard tool (we use Power BI), and clear writing for readers who are not technical. Tableau is nice to have, not required.

Closing date: 7 November.
files.background.md:
Priya Raman. Reporting analyst at Tessel Transit, a regional bus operator, for 3 years 2 months.

- Wrote the SQL behind the weekly ridership report used by 11 route managers; its run time went from 40 minutes to 6.
- Rebuilt the monthly punctuality dashboard in Power BI. Route managers now use it in place of a 14-page PDF.
- Found that 2.1% of fare-tap records were double counted when two data feeds were joined. Fixed the join, corrected 8 months of figures and wrote a one-page note for managers explaining the change.
- Since 2023 volunteers on Saturdays at the Aldgate Road library homework club. Mention it in one line, do not make it the story.

Has not used Tableau.

checks.note: addressed to the manager the posting names
SQL result kept with its units
if Tableau comes up, it is said she has not used it

checks.pattern: (?i)\b(?:enthusiastic|passionate|passion for|highly motivated|detail-oriented|fast learner|ideal candidate|excited (?:to|about) (?:apply|contribute|the opportunity)|express my (?:interest|enthusiasm))\b

(?i)hope (?:this|you)[^.\n]{0,40}(?:finds you|well)|don'?t hesitate|do not hesitate|reach out|any inconvenience|valued customer|sincerely apologi[sz]e|look forward to hearing|(?:thank you|thanks) (?:so much )?for your (?:patience|understanding|time and consideration|continued)|first and foremost|i wanted to (?:reach out|provide)|as a (?:result|reminder),?
checks.note: no stock email opener or closer
The deliverable goes straight to its reader and the notes hold every fact the text needs, so no gap marker belongs in the saved file; a question for the author goes in the reply.
no fill-in placeholder in text for a reader
the file is the deliverable, not a reply with a lead-in or notes about it

controls.name: good
controls.output:
Dear Hannah Okoye,

I am applying for the Data Analyst role at Northgate Library Network. For 3 years 2 months I have been a reporting analyst at Tessel Transit, a regional bus operator, and the work you describe is the work I do now.

You need monthly usage reports that branch managers will read. At Tessel I wrote the SQL behind the weekly ridership report that 11 route managers use. Its run time went from 40 minutes to 6, so managers get the figures when they need them. I also rebuilt our monthly punctuality dashboard in Power BI. Route managers now use it in place of a 14-page PDF.

Your posting also asks for clean joins across data from different systems, such as your loans system and the door counters. I have done this under pressure. I found that 2.1% of our fare-tap records were double counted when two data feeds were joined. I fixed the join and corrected 8 months of figures. Then I wrote a one-page note that told managers what had changed and why, because a corrected number that nobody understands loses trust faster than a wrong one.

That note is the part of the job I care about most: explaining a result to people who are not technical, and answering a question from a board in plain words.

I have not used Tableau, and I see it is a nice-to-have rather than a requirement. Power BI is the tool I know well, and I expect to pick up another dashboard tool as quickly as I picked up that one.

Since 2023 I have also volunteered on Saturdays at the homework club at Aldgate Road library.

I would welcome the chance to talk about how this fits your 14 branches. The posting closes on 7 November.

Priya Raman
